_**Assistant (gpt-4o-mini)**_

In Django templates, string comparisons are case-sensitive. This means that `"Ja"` and `"ja"` are considered different strings. If you want the condition to be case-insensitive, you can use the `|lower` filter to convert both sides of the comparison to lowercase. Here's how you can modify your template code:

```django
{% if item.aircraft|lower == "ja" %}
```

This way, regardless of whether `item.aircraft` is `"Ja"`, `"ja"`, or any other case variation, the condition will evaluate to `True` if it matches `"ja"` in a case-insensitive manner.
